question: Under Mississippi Code § 73-35-8, an applicant may qualify for a Mississippi nonresident real estate license under any of three specific categories. Which of the following is NOT one of those categories?
choice_a: A person who is already licensed as a broker in another state
choice_b: A broker-salesperson or salesperson affiliated with a resident or nonresident Mississippi broker
choice_c: A person who has never held any real estate license in any state but simply wishes to practice in Mississippi
choice_d: A nonresident who applies for a broker's license and will maintain an office in Mississippi
explanation: Section 73-35-8(1) defines exactly three paths to a Mississippi nonresident's license: (a) an individual already licensed as a broker in another state, (b) a broker-salesperson or salesperson affiliated with a resident or nonresident Mississippi broker, or (c) a nonresident applying for a broker's license who will maintain a Mississippi office. There is no category allowing someone with no real estate license anywhere to obtain a Mississippi nonresident license -- nonresident licensure is built on top of an existing brokerage relationship or an out-of-state license, not on a blank slate.

question: A nonresident broker who wants a Mississippi nonresident broker's license but does not intend to keep an office in Mississippi may still qualify, provided that the broker:
choice_a: Pays double the standard license fee to offset the lack of an in-state office
choice_b: Appoints a Mississippi resident as co-broker of record on every transaction
choice_c: Limits nonresident practice in Mississippi to transactions valued under $250,000
choice_d: Is regularly and actively engaged in the real estate business and maintains a place of business in the other state
explanation: Section 73-35-8(1) expressly states that a nonresident broker need not maintain a place of business within Mississippi, provided he is regularly and actively engaged in the real estate business and maintains a place of business in the other state. There is no fee surcharge, mandatory co-broker, or transaction-value cap tied to this option -- the statute's only conditions are active engagement in the business and a genuine office in the broker's home state.

question: By filing the statement of irrevocable consent required under § 73-35-8(2), a nonresident applicant for a Mississippi real estate license agrees to what?
choice_a: Having legal actions served on the licensee, through the Real Estate Commission or the Secretary of State, treated as valid and binding as if personal service had been made on the licensee in Mississippi, and consenting to attend commission hearings at a place the commission designates
choice_b: Automatic revocation of the license after five years unless the licensee physically relocates to Mississippi
choice_c: Waiver of any right to appeal an adverse decision of the commission
choice_d: Payment of an annual nonresident surcharge to the Mississippi Attorney General's office
explanation: Section 73-35-8(2) requires every nonresident applicant to file a statement of irrevocable consent that legal actions may be commenced against him in the proper Mississippi court, with service made by the Secretary of State or the commission (or its chief executive officer), and that such service 'shall be taken in all courts to be valid and binding as if personal service had been made upon the nonresident licensee in this state.' The same subsection requires the nonresident to consent to have any § 73-35-23 hearings held at a place the commission designates. There is no five-year relocation clause, appeal waiver, or AG surcharge in the statute.

question: Under § 73-35-8(3), what must occur before a default judgment can be taken against a nonresident licensee who was served through the Real Estate Commission?
choice_a: The commission must first obtain a Chancery Court order authorizing default
choice_b: At least thirty days must pass after the process or pleading was mailed by certified mail to the licensee's last-known principal address, supported by an affidavit or certification from the commission or its executive officer confirming the mailing
choice_c: The plaintiff must post a bond equal to the full amount of claimed damages
choice_d: The licensee's home-state real estate commission must provide written consent to the default
explanation: Section 73-35-8(3) requires duplicate copies of any process or pleading to be filed -- one with the commission and one sent by certified mail to the nonresident licensee's last-known principal address. No default may be taken except upon an affidavit or certification from the commission (or its executive officer) that the mailing was made, and no default judgment may be entered until thirty days after that mailing. Nothing in the statute requires a separate court order, a plaintiff's bond, or home-state commission consent.

question: In addition to the consent-to-service requirement, what else must a nonresident license applicant sign under § 73-35-8(4)?
choice_a: A $10,000 surety bond payable to the State of Mississippi
choice_b: A certification that the applicant has completed 40 hours of Mississippi-specific coursework beyond what residents must take
choice_c: An agreement to cooperate with any investigation of the applicant's real estate brokerage activities that the commission may undertake
choice_d: A letter of good standing from the National Association of REALTORS®
explanation: Section 73-35-8(4) requires the nonresident applicant to sign an agreement to cooperate with any investigation of the applicant's real estate brokerage activities that the commission may undertake. Mississippi's license law imposes no separate surety bond, no extra 40-hour Mississippi-only coursework requirement, and no NAR good-standing letter for nonresident applicants.

question: Which statement correctly describes the overall qualification standard for a Mississippi nonresident license applicant under § 73-35-8(5) and (6)?
choice_a: Nonresident applicants are exempt from Mississippi's background investigation and examination requirements altogether
choice_b: Nonresident applicants need only submit a photocopy of their home-state license, with no other supporting documentation
choice_c: Nonresident applicants may only ever qualify for salesperson status in Mississippi, never for a broker's license
choice_d: The nonresident applicant must qualify in all respects the same as a Mississippi resident applicant -- including background investigation, examination, and fees -- except for the residency requirement and (where approved) equivalent pre-licensing education, and must also furnish certification of licensure from every state in which the applicant has held a real estate license
explanation: Section 73-35-8(5) requires each nonresident applicant to qualify 'in all respects, including education, background investigation, examination and fees, as an applicant who is a resident of Mississippi,' with the sole exceptions being the residency requirement and approved equivalent pre-licensing education. Section 73-35-8(6) additionally requires a certification from the executive officer of the real estate commission in the applicant's home state, plus disclosure of all states in which the applicant has held a license along with certifications of licensure from each. Nonresidents are not exempt from background checks or exams, and § 73-35-8(1) expressly contemplates nonresident broker's licenses, not just salesperson licenses.

question: Before conducting business as a nonresident broker in Mississippi, § 73-35-8(7) requires the applicant/broker to:
choice_a: Obtain an appropriate Mississippi license for the firm through which the applicant intends to operate as a broker
choice_b: Register the operating firm as a foreign corporation with the Mississippi Secretary of State only, with no involvement from the Real Estate Commission
choice_c: File Articles of Incorporation directly with the Mississippi Real Estate Commission
choice_d: Obtain a separate nonresident license for every Mississippi county in which the firm intends to transact business
explanation: Section 73-35-8(7) states plainly: 'The applicant/broker shall obtain an appropriate Mississippi license for the firm through which he intends to operate as a broker.' Mississippi licensing runs through the commission, not merely a Secretary of State foreign-entity filing, and there is no county-by-county nonresident licensing scheme or requirement to file Articles of Incorporation with the commission.

question: Once licensed, how do a Mississippi nonresident broker's or salesperson's continuing education (CE) obligations compare to those of a resident licensee, under § 73-35-8(8)?
choice_a: Nonresidents are fully exempt from Mississippi CE because their home state's CE requirements are presumed to satisfy Mississippi's
choice_b: Any nonresident broker, broker-salesperson, and salesperson must meet Mississippi continuing education requirements after becoming licensed, just as any resident licensee must
choice_c: Nonresidents need complete only half the CE hours required of residents
choice_d: CE is optional for nonresidents but mandatory for residents
explanation: Section 73-35-8(8) states: 'Any nonresident broker, broker-salesperson and salesperson shall meet Mississippi continuing education requirements after becoming licensed just as any resident licensee.' There is no home-state CE substitution, no reduced-hours accommodation, and CE is mandatory for both residents and nonresidents alike.

question: Mississippi Code § 73-35-7 authorizes the commission to exempt an out-of-state applicant from Mississippi's pre-licensing educational requirements, in whole or in part. Under what condition may the commission grant that exemption?
choice_a: Only for applicants who are licensed attorneys in their home state
choice_b: Whenever the applicant simply requests the exemption in writing
choice_c: Only if the applicant's home-state pre-licensing education requirements are determined by the commission to be equivalent to Mississippi's, AND that other state extends the same educational exemption privilege to Mississippi real estate licensees
choice_d: Only if the applicant completes an online refresher course certified by ARELLO
explanation: Section 73-35-7 provides that the commission 'is authorized to exempt from such pre-licensing educational requirements, in whole or in part, a real estate licensee of another state who desires to obtain a license under this chapter, provided that the pre-licensing educational requirements in the other state are determined by the commission to be equivalent to pre-licensing educational requirements in this state and provided that such state extends this same privilege or exemption to Mississippi real estate licensees.' Both the equivalency finding and the reciprocal grant by the other state are required -- one without the other is not enough.

question: Mississippi Code § 73-35-13(6) allows the Real Estate Commission to exempt an out-of-state licensee from taking Mississippi's written examination. Which TWO conditions must both be satisfied for the commission to grant this exemption?
choice_a: The applicant must be at least 40 years old and have a minimum of ten years of brokerage experience
choice_b: The applicant must still pass a shortened 20-question Mississippi law exam regardless of home-state licensure status
choice_c: The applicant's home state must share a border with Mississippi
choice_d: The examination administered in the applicant's home state must be determined by the commission to be equivalent to the examination given in Mississippi, AND that other state must extend this same examination-exemption privilege to Mississippi real estate licensees
explanation: Section 73-35-13(6) provides: 'The commission is authorized to exempt from such examination, in whole or in part, a real estate licensee of another state who desires to obtain a license under this chapter, provided that the examination administered in the other state is determined by the commission to be equivalent to such examination given in this state and provided that such other state extends this same privilege or exemption to Mississippi real estate licensees.' This is Mississippi's core license-for-license reciprocity mechanism: it requires both an equivalency finding by MREC AND a matching, mutual exemption extended by the other state to Mississippi licensees. There is no age/experience threshold, no shortened substitute exam, and no border requirement.

question: Under § 73-35-11, a real estate broker licensed in another state who holds no Mississippi license may lawfully participate in a Mississippi real estate transaction only if:
choice_a: The out-of-state broker cooperates with a Mississippi-licensed broker, with any resulting commission or fee stated on a form filed with the commission reflecting the compensation to be paid to the Mississippi broker
choice_b: The out-of-state broker first registers as a foreign business entity with the Mississippi Secretary of State
choice_c: The transaction's total value is under $100,000
choice_d: The out-of-state broker first obtains a temporary 90-day Mississippi salesperson's license
explanation: Section 73-35-11 makes it unlawful for anyone not licensed as a Mississippi resident or nonresident broker/salesperson to perform brokerage acts in Mississippi, but it carves out one exception: 'a licensed broker of another state who does not hold a Mississippi real estate license may cooperate with a licensed broker of this state provided that any commission or fee resulting from such cooperative negotiation shall be stated on a form filed with the commission reflecting the compensation to be paid to the Mississippi broker.' There is no Secretary of State foreign-entity registration, transaction-value cap, or 90-day temporary license pathway in this section.

question: When a Mississippi broker enters into a cooperative agreement with an out-of-state broker under § 73-35-11, what filing obligation does the Mississippi broker have, and what does the out-of-state broker agree to by signing the agreement?
choice_a: The Mississippi broker must notify the buyer's lender within 24 hours; the out-of-state broker agrees to waive any right to commission
choice_b: The Mississippi broker must file a copy of the written cooperative agreement with the commission within ten days; by signing, the out-of-state broker agrees to abide by Mississippi law and the commission's rules and regulations and consents that civil actions may be brought against him in any Mississippi court of competent jurisdiction
choice_c: The Mississippi broker must co-sign the out-of-state broker's state income tax return; the out-of-state broker agrees to relocate to Mississippi within one year
choice_d: The Mississippi broker must obtain MREC's advance approval before ever showing the property; the out-of-state broker agrees to forfeit all escrow rights
explanation: Section 73-35-11 states: 'Whenever a Mississippi broker enters into a cooperative agreement under this section, the Mississippi broker shall file within ten (10) days with the commission a copy of each such written agreement. By signing the agreement, the nonresident broker who is not licensed in this state agrees to abide by Mississippi law, and the rules and regulations of the commission; and further agrees that civil actions may be commenced against him in any court of competent jurisdiction in any county of this state in which a claim may arise.' None of the other described obligations (lender notice, tax co-signing, MREC pre-approval of showings, escrow forfeiture) appear in the statute.

question: Under § 73-35-11, what advertising rule applies when Mississippi property is marketed under a cooperative agreement involving a nonresident, unlicensed out-of-state broker?
choice_a: Only the nonresident broker's name may appear in any advertisement of the property
choice_b: Advertisements for such cooperative listings need not identify either broker by name
choice_c: The Mississippi broker's name and telephone number must appear in the advertisement and be given equal prominence with the name of the nonresident broker
choice_d: All advertising of the property is prohibited once a cooperative agreement is in place
explanation: Section 73-35-11 requires that 'in all advertising of real estate located in Mississippi, the name and telephone number of the Mississippi broker shall appear and shall be given equal prominence with the name of the nonresident broker who is not licensed in this state.' The statute affirmatively requires disclosure of the Mississippi broker with equal billing -- it does not permit the nonresident broker's name alone, allow anonymous advertising, or ban advertising outright.

question: Regarding liability, verification, and escrow duties in a § 73-35-11 cooperative agreement, which statement is accurate?
choice_a: The Mississippi Real Estate Commission, not the Mississippi broker, is responsible for verifying the cooperating broker's out-of-state license status
choice_b: The Mississippi broker bears no liability whatsoever for the cooperating out-of-state broker's conduct
choice_c: Earnest money in a cooperative agreement must always be held by the out-of-state broker, never the Mississippi broker
choice_d: The Mississippi broker must confirm the cooperating broker is licensed as a broker in another state, remains liable for the cooperating broker's acts as well as his own arising from the cooperative agreement, and must hold all earnest money from the transaction in escrow unless both buyer and seller agree in writing to relieve him of that duty
explanation: Section 73-35-11 provides that 'the Mississippi broker shall be liable for all acts of the above cooperating broker, as well as for his own acts, arising from the execution of any cooperative agreement,' that 'the Mississippi broker shall determine that the cooperating broker is licensed as a broker in another state,' and that 'all earnest money pertaining to a cooperative agreement must be held in escrow by the Mississippi broker unless both the buyer and seller agree in writing to relieve the Mississippi broker of this responsibility.' Verification, liability, and (by default) escrow custody all rest with the Mississippi broker, not the commission or the out-of-state broker.

question: Mississippi's real estate license law (Title 73, Chapter 35) does not contain a freestanding 'subdivided lands' or land-developer registration act comparable to those found in some other states. Which of the following, however, IS a real, confirmed authority the Mississippi Real Estate Commission holds specifically over out-of-state developers, under § 73-35-35(1)?
choice_a: Authority to adopt rules and regulations regulating the sale of timesharing and condominium properties within Mississippi, and also the sale of timesharing and condominium properties located in other states when those properties are sold to Mississippi residents
choice_b: Authority to require every out-of-state land developer to post a $1,000,000 bond with the State Treasurer before marketing any Mississippi property
choice_c: Authority to void any out-of-state subdivision plat that has not been separately re-recorded in Mississippi
choice_d: Authority to impose Mississippi ad valorem property taxes directly on an out-of-state developer's unsold inventory
explanation: Section 73-35-35(1) grants the commission authority to 'adopt such rules and regulations as it deems appropriate to regulate the sale of timesharing and condominium properties within the State of Mississippi and the sale of timesharing and condominium properties in other states to residents of Mississippi.' This is the specific, verified hook Chapter 35 gives MREC over out-of-state developers -- it reaches timeshare and condominium sales aimed at Mississippi residents even when the project sits outside the state. No provision was found authorizing a blanket developer bond, plat-voiding power, or direct property taxation by MREC; those would fall (if at all) under other statutory schemes, not Chapter 35's license law.
